newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines in dlr repo pact with Bank of China.
newsitem.headline: Philippines in dlr repo pact with Bank of China.

text.p: The Philippine Central Bank is scheduled to sign on Tuesday a dollar repurchase agreement with Bank of China, Central Bank governor Gabriel Singson said on Monday.
The repo agreement is the seventh to be signed by the Central Bank.
The agreement would provide the central banks with standby liquidity funds that could be tapped in case of massive withdrawal of dollars.

"By offering their U.S. Treasury holdings with a promise to buy the same at a later date, participating central banks can raise the needed cash without liquidating their securities holdings," the Central Bank said in a statement.
The Central Bank had earlier signed similar agreements with the central banks of Hong Kong, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapore and Japan.
Singson said the standby fund and a comfortable level of foreign exchange reserves "will further equip the Central Bank in its effort to deal with any possible financial market disturbances."
The Central Bank had $11.8 billion in gross international reserves by the end of last year, up from $7.7 billion by end-1995.
